# Production refund replay investigation

## Active request path

Production selects `credit-v2`, `settlement-log`, and a 900 second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). The HTTP `postCredit` handler takes the caller supplied `x-replay-key` header and request body and passes both to `makeCredit` ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1-L2)).

`makeCredit` claims the key before appending a credit. If the claim reports an existing request, it returns that claim's stored receipt and does not call `appendCredit`; otherwise it appends the credit ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1-L3)). The claim calls `ctx.store.claimUnique` with `namespace: ctx.tenant`, the header value as `key`, and `ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` as `expiresSeconds` ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1)). Appending calls `ctx.store.commitCredit(ticket, body)` ([packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). The implementation path is `packages/http/credits.mjs` → `packages/accounting/credit.mjs` → `packages/settlement/replay.mjs` → `packages/settlement/log.mjs`.

The accepted ADR identifies the live `credit-v2` claim as a tenant namespaced `settlement-log` claim that survives worker restarts, and says a matching request within the window receives the stored receipt ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L1-L2)). Thus a client retry after a disconnect is protected when it sends the same replay key for the same tenant while the claim remains valid. The key originates with the client; the handler does not generate it ([packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L2)).

## Window and limits

The configured protection window is 900 seconds (15 minutes) ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)). The operations note says the record expires after that window and a second credit is possible after expiry; it reports no deployment measurements, so actual duplicate credit incidence is unknown ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L1-L2)).

The archived rollout describes an experimental `credit-v1` process memory key with a 60 second window and explicitly says it is superseded ([docs/archive/refund-rollout.md](docs/archive/refund-rollout.md#L1-L2)). A legacy in-memory map is present, but it is not on the traced HTTP path ([packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs](packages/legacy/refund-memory.mjs#L1); [packages/http/credits.mjs](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1); [packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1-L3)). Its restart behavior and 60 second value do not describe the selected production driver ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs#L1)).

The repository exposes `ctx.store.claimUnique` and `ctx.store.commitCredit` as calls, without their underlying implementation in this path ([packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1); [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). The accepted ADR supplies the durability claim, but the repository evidence does not establish the store's transaction or crash recovery details, exact expiry boundary, behavior for a missing or changed replay key, or measured incidence in production ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2); [docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)).

Production selects `credit-v2` with `settlement-log` storage and a 900-second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs](config/production.mjs)). `makeCredit` claims the key before issuing a credit. The claim uses `ctx.tenant` as its namespace and `ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` as its expiry; an existing ticket returns its stored receipt, while a new ticket proceeds to `appendCredit`, which calls `ctx.store.commitCredit` ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs](packages/accounting/credit.mjs), [packages/settlement/replay.mjs](packages/settlement/replay.mjs), [packages/settlement/log.mjs](packages/settlement/log.mjs)). After the 900-second record expires, another credit is possible ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md)). Actual duplicate-credit incidence is unknown: this repository has no deployment measurements ([docs/ops/late-replay.md](docs/ops/late-replay.md)). # Production refund replay protection

Production selects the `credit-v2` refund driver, `settlement-log` storage, and a 900-second deduplication window ([config/production.mjs:1](config/production.mjs#L1)). The HTTP credit handler reads the caller-supplied `x-replay-key` header and passes it with the request body to `makeCredit` ([packages/http/credits.mjs:1](packages/http/credits.mjs#L1), [packages/http/credits.mjs:2](packages/http/credits.mjs#L2)).

`makeCredit` first claims that key. The claim calls `ctx.store.claimUnique` with `namespace: ctx.tenant`, the supplied key, and `expiresSeconds: ctx.config.dedupWindowSeconds` ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs:1](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L1), [packages/accounting/credit.mjs:3](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3), [packages/settlement/replay.mjs:1](packages/settlement/replay.mjs#L1)). Thus the replay key is isolated by tenant. If the claim reports an existing ticket, `makeCredit` returns its stored receipt and does not call the credit append path. Otherwise it calls `appendCredit`, which passes the ticket and body to `ctx.store.commitCredit` ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs:2](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L2), [packages/accounting/credit.mjs:3](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3), [packages/settlement/log.mjs:1](packages/settlement/log.mjs#L1)). A client repeating the same key within the window should therefore receive the earlier receipt instead of a second credit, including when the repeat follows a disconnect; the code does not show special disconnect handling ([packages/accounting/credit.mjs:3](packages/accounting/credit.mjs#L3), [docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2)).

The accepted ADR identifies the live settlement-log uniqueness claim as durable across worker restarts and confirms the tenant namespace and stored-receipt behavior ([docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:1](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L1), [docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md:2](docs/adr/017-refund-replays.md#L2)). The 900-second production value is 15 minutes; after the replay record expires, a second credit is possible ([config/production.mjs:1](config/production.mjs#L1), [docs/ops/late-replay.md:2](docs/ops/late-replay.md#L2)).
